findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether each transcribed child `description` must include a parseable `## Acceptance Criteria` block (so the roster is coverage-bearing for G3), or explicitly accept the title-only roster fallback and note that G3 gold labels are then judged from the children_block prose rather than the roster ACs.
evidence: build_sibling_roster (pass1.py:112-129) parses each child's `## Acceptance Criteria` from description and 'A child with no parseable ## Acceptance Criteria keeps its bare line, so the roster degrades to the historical title-only shape'

pass1_container instruction (passes.py:399): 'An absence is a finding only if NO sibling in the roster covers it' — G3's fire/no-fire on covered-by-named-consumer cases depends on the roster surfacing the covering child/consumer

Plan asserts 'the gold label (expect) of every case is unchanged by construction' but grounds that only in the input prose, not in what the roster (built from child descriptions) will actually expose to the model
findings.finding: The plan specifies children as {ticket_id, title, description} transcribed from input prose but does not address whether each child's description must carry a parseable `## Acceptance Criteria` block for the sibling roster to be rich enough for G3's coverage cross-check to reproduce the case's gold label.
findings.location: Approach / Scope — 'The children are transcribed, not invented' and 'children list ... {ticket_id, title, description}'
scenarios: A G3-R-uncovered-ac case where thin, title-only child descriptions leave the roster unable to show the reviewer that the parent's idempotency AC is genuinely uncovered vs merely absent from titles
A G3-FP-covered-by-named-consumer case where the covering child's coverage is stated only in title-level prose, so the roster degrades to title-only and G3 mis-fires against the gold pass label

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` in Scope as either an update target or an explicit, justified out-of-scope item, since the fix contradicts its `corpus_note` and its recorded errored container G3 rows.
evidence: provider_parity_results.json:3 corpus_note: "...were excluded as errored pairs, so the SCORED pair set is the 28 items of corpus_digest_current, which is what the selector now returns after that exclusion was added."
provider_parity_results.json:390-418 records G3-FP-covered-by-named-consumer-rebar and G3-R-uncovered-ac-rebar as {errored:true, decision:"dropped"} under spec plan-review-container
This file is loaded and re-scored offline by test_recorded_live_results_re_score_against_the_same_parity_bar (test_provider_parity.py:474) via pp.recheck_recorded
The plan's Scope lists ONLY plan-review-container.eval.yaml and tests/unit/test_provider_parity.py, and states 'No source change' — the results artifact is not mentioned
findings.finding: The committed recorded-results artifact `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json` is a consumer the fix makes stale but is neither enumerated in Scope nor explicitly ruled out-of-scope: its `corpus_note` narrates the container G3 cases being excluded ("the SCORED pair set is the 28 items"), and it records both `plan-review-container` G3 cases as errored/dropped — the very outcome the fix reverses.
findings.location: Scope section ("No source change... only those two files") vs src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/provider_parity_results.json:3,13,29-42,390-418
scenarios: After the fix, live select_corpus(eligible_cases()) returns 30 items and treats the container cases as scoreable, while the committed artifact still records them as errored and its corpus_note describes them as permanently excluded — the repo's own record now contradicts the fixed behavior.
A future reader diffing the artifact against the live selector (corpus_digest_current is dead data no code recomputes) is misled about which corpus is current.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope bullet stating the recorded results JSON is DELIBERATELY left unchanged (a historical live run re-scored by dropping errored pairs; recheck_recorded reads the committed rows and never recomputes the corpus, so no test breaks) — or, if the record should reflect the fixed corpus, note it will be regenerated. Either way, name the file so AC-6's `git diff --stat` check is unambiguous.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an offline assertion (in test_plan_review_evals.py or test_provider_parity.py) that _run_criterion_case for a fixed container case does NOT raise 'needs a non-empty children list', proving the pre-model fixture-validation raise is cleared — not merely that the case is eligible.
evidence: Problem: 'ALL 12 cases ... none can be executed through run_case'
Evidence: 'raised ValueError ... on BOTH arms at ALL 3 epochs, before any model call'
ACs prove eligibility (carries children, appears in eligible_cases, corpus==30) but none invoke _run_criterion_case to confirm the raise is no longer reached
findings.finding: The problem statement is that container cases 'cannot be executed through run_case' because _run_criterion_case raises a ValueError before any model call when children is empty. Every AC and test proves the cases are now ELIGIBLE (carry a non-empty children list and appear in eligible_cases()), but no criterion confirms that _run_criterion_case actually gets PAST the fixture-validation raise for one of these cases. Since the Evidence section establishes the raise fires 'before any model call' (i.e. offline), an offline assertion that a fixed container case no longer raises 'needs a non-empty children list' is achievable and would directly prove the stated bug is fixed.
scenarios: A children entry is added but is malformed such that _run_criterion_case's validation still raises even though _runnable/eligible_cases (which only check for a non-empty list) admit it — eligibility passes green while the actual run still fails
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that calls _run_criterion_case for one G3/G4 container case with the loaded fixture and stubs the model call, asserting the pre-call ValueError is not raised.
